newsitem.title: UK: Stocks fall in London, rebound in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall in London, rebound in Tokyo.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - Leading British shares slipped as growing worries about higher interest rates and fears of a protracted decline on Wall Street sent investors running for cover. The benchmark FTSE 100 share index closed 11.5 points lower at 4,236.6, having fallen as low as 4,219.0.

FRANKFURT - Shares plunged in afternoon electronic trade, after jittery markets reacted sharply to an unwelcome fall on Wall Street and surrendered ground gained in bourse trade. Shares fell after a lower opening on the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street, and the IBIS DAX index of 30 blue-chip German shares ended the day at 3,210.94 points, down 70.52 points or 2.15 percent. This was one of the sharpest falls in the index since November and meant the index more than lost the ground it made up in bourse trade, when the DAX index ended up 5.98 points at 3,301.91 points.

PARIS - Shares finished with another sizeable loss, after an attempt to rebound from Tuesday's 2.82 percent drop lost momentum. Traders said it was hard to call the market's direction as prices were highly sensitive to gyrations on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 51.54 points, or 2 percent, at 2,530.20.

ZURICH - Shares broke from an early rise, ending weaker in quiet trade as a technical reaction to Tuesday's slump wore off during the course of the day. The all-share SPI was down 4.64 points at 2,851.59.

TOKYO - Stocks ended moderately higher, helped by selective buying of shares with good earnings prospects. Mixed results from the "tankan" corporate sentiment survey released in the morning had a limited impact on the market. The 225-share Nikkei average climbed 167.71 points or 0.94 percent to 18,037.30.

HONG KONG - Stocks staged a rebound after three days of losses, lifted mainly by the banking sector while other sectors remained subdued amid interest rate uncertainty and worries in the property market. The Hang Seng Index closed with a gain of 62.13 points, or 0.51 percent, at 12,136.32. Over the previous three sessions, the index had lost 758.34 points.

SYDNEY - Stocks eased off their high's and the key index only just remained in positive territory as investors remained nervous about Wall Street. A sharp fall in leading bank stock Westpac also put pressure on the market. The All Ordinaries index rose 3.0 points at 2,355.2.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares edged up as the market gave out a collective sigh of relief after a modest overnight gain on Wall Street followed two days of successive heavy losses. But most players are still wary of recent jitters on the Dow and the local market came off its highs as the afternoon wore on and U.S.-inspired nervousness grew. The industrials index ended up 5.2 points at 8,179.8, the all-share index put on 18.7 points to 6,981.1. The golds index also added 5.2 points to 1,297.5.
